recognize_zh: 周邊血抹片中，中性球內塞滿多個橢圓形、周圍有透明暈的酵母菌，並可見出芽（箭頭）與延長的假菌絲（pseudohyphae），細胞外也有成串出芽的菌體，符合念珠菌血症（Candida albicans 敗血症）。
features: Neutrophils containing multiple oval, basophilic yeast cells (about 3-6 µm) surrounded by clear halos
Budding yeasts (arrows) and elongated sausage-shaped pseudohyphal forms
Extracellular chain of budding yeast/pseudohyphae between red cells
Host neutrophils show coarse toxic granulation and cytoplasmic vacuolation
Thrombocytopenia with few platelets; red cells show mild hypochromia
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows neutrophils engorged with multiple intracellular oval yeast forms, each surrounded by a clear halo, together with elongated pseudohyphal forms and an extracellular chain of budding yeasts. The neutrophils show toxic granulation and vacuolation. Platelets are reduced and red cells are mildly hypochromic. Findings are consistent with fungemia due to Candida species, in keeping with the reported Candida albicans line-related sepsis; detection on a routine smear indicates a high organism burden.

ddx.vs: Histoplasma yeasts are smaller (2-4 µm), uniform, with narrow-based budding at most and never form pseudohyphae.
Malassezia forms smaller yeasts with broad-based collarette budding in patients receiving lipid infusions and does not form true pseudohyphal chains in blood.
Talaromyces yeasts divide by binary fission with a central septum rather than budding.

ddx.dx: Bacterial rods (e.g., Clostridium or Bacillus) in neutrophils
ddx.vs: Bacteria are much smaller and slender, without the oval budding cells and clear halos of yeast.
